title: Haiqu Releases AgenticOS to Plan and Check Quantum Research
source_used: The Quantum Insider (full text of Haiqu's press release read)
key_facts: Haiqu, a quantum software company, unveiled AgenticOS, teams of AI agents that help quantum researchers plan a project from question to a hardware-ready experiment.

The agents review literature, do first-principles mathematical derivations, assess quantum feasibility and check results against classical baselines, tests, critic agents and human review; scientists decide what gets locked.
In a chemistry study accepted at a NeurIPS 2026 workshop in Paris, four of 10 runs of leading AI agents without AgenticOS ignored an explicit setup instruction.
With AgenticOS, the same models held to the approved protocol and produced a simulated quantum result within about 3.4% of the exact diagonalization reference.
AgenticOS was used on a 3-by-3 grid version of the Hubbard model (a model used to study high-temperature superconductivity), ran on an IBM quantum computer and cut circuit depth by 75%.

Named in the release: Mykola Maksymenko, co-founder and CTO of Haiqu; Richard Givhan, co-founder and CEO of Haiqu. AgenticOS is available now to enterprise R&D teams on request; academics can apply for free access.
quote_evidence: On their own, four of 10 agent runs ignored an explicit setup instruction, resulting in widely different answers.
Using Haiqu’s AgenticOS, the same models held to the approved protocol from start to finish and produced a simulated quantum result within approximately 3.4% of the exact diagonalization reference.
why_it_matters_hint: A company product launch with its own test results; the tool's claims have no outside check reported.
notes: Joint company press release carried by The Quantum Insider; no outlet reporting. Source credited to the issuer, Haiqu; url is the page read. Pool score 5 kept.
